narration: First, the input image I is fed into the visual encoder CLIP V to extract spatial visual feature map F_v.
Concurrently, the input prompt text T containing target categories is encoded by CLIP L into text feature vector F_l.
The visual features F_v and linguistic features F_l are correlated to generate multi-channel visual-linguistic correlation maps C_{v&l}.
Inside the ESC-Block, the correlation maps enter the Pseudo Prompt Generator (PPG) to produce candidate point and mask pseudo-prompts.
The Segment Anything Model (SAM) Block processes the visual feature map F_v guided by the pseudo-prompts to produce refined visual features F prime v.
The Vision-Language Fusion (VLF) Block combines the refined visual features, original correlation maps, and text embeddings into refined correlation maps C prime v&l.
Across N recurring ESC-Blocks, the refined features pass to the decoder to produce the final segmented prediction mask M.
